subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed device.publicKey/signature bounds and per-IP device-signature pre-auth lockout as the gateway security boundary for connect handshakes?
rationale: The code path is security-sensitive and changes unauthenticated gateway behavior, protocol validation, and availability under failed device-bearing browser-origin handshakes; automation can review mechanics but cannot own that security/availability policy choice.

options.title: Accept layered hardening
options.body: Approve the schema bounds, shape pre-checks, and pre-crypto limiter as the intended mitigation, then merge after normal owner review.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Ask for adjusted bounds, limiter scope, or PoC placement while preserving the early gate before createPublicKey and verify.

options.title: Pause for replacement design
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want a different gateway auth architecture rather than extending the current limiter model.

recommendation.title: Accept layered hardening
recommendation.body: Approve the schema bounds, shape pre-checks, and pre-crypto limiter as the intended mitigation, then merge after normal owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns much of the current device-auth and gateway auth history and has merged adjacent gateway security work.
